findings.title: DOMAIN: normalize_url upper-cases scheme and authority for every scheme, not only http(s) - unsafe for custom/deep-link schemes
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-qr/src/url.rs:60-99 (normalize_url); pinned by the test case at url.rs:139 ("ebk+app://Open/Item" -> "EBK+APP://OPEN/Item")
findings.evidence: Scratch probe against the crate: normalize_url("ebk+app://Open/Item") = "EBK+APP://OPEN/Item"; "kobo://Library/open?id=Abc" -> "KOBO://LIBRARY/open?id=Abc"; "intent://Scan/#Intent;..." -> "INTENT://SCAN/#Intent;...". RFC 3986 calls the host case-insensitive, but real consumers do not for non-special schemes: Node 22 (WHATWG URL) gives new URL("ebk+app://Open/Item").host == "Open" and new URL("EBK+APP://OPEN/Item").host == "OPEN" (opaque host, case preserved), so the rewritten URL is a different URL to any WHATWG-based handler. The project's own research (docs/research/notes/ereader-ux.ecosystems.md:134-135,186) names opds://authorize/ and opds://example.com/user/shelf deep links, where the 'host' is a keyword an app compares literally. From memory of the Android docs (web-search budget was exhausted, not re-verified): intent-filter scheme AND host matching are case-sensitive, so an upper-cased custom scheme may not resolve and an upper-cased https host will not match an App Link filter (falls back to the browser). Separately, the doc comment states as fact "Phone cameras resolve HTTPS://EBK.EXAMPLE/... exactly like the lower-case form" while docs/research/notes/ereader-ux.ux.md:34 and :300 mark exactly this as unverified ('test on real phones'); CLAUDE.md rule 8 wants that caveat in the code comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Only rewrite when the scheme is http or https (optionally ws/wss/ftp, the WHATWG 'special' schemes whose host is a domain). Return every other URL byte for byte (or at most leave the decision to the caller via a flag). Replace the test expectation for ebk+app:// accordingly, and reword the phone-camera sentence as 'expected per RFC 3986 / ZXing, not yet verified on stock iOS/Android cameras'.

findings.title: DOMAIN: a backslash in an http(s) URL makes normalize_url upper-case what every browser treats as the PATH
findings.evidence: Probe: normalize_url("https://ebk.example\\k\\abc") = Ok("HTTPS://EBK.EXAMPLE\\K\\ABC"); normalize_url("https://ebk.example\\@evil.example/Path") = Ok("HTTPS://ebk.example\\@EVIL.EXAMPLE/Path"). Node 22 WHATWG parser: new URL("https://ebk.example\\k\\abc").pathname == "/k/abc" but for the normalised string it is "/K/ABC"; for the second case the path changes from /@evil.example/Path to /@EVIL.EXAMPLE/Path. A 400 000-input fuzz (scratch) found 701 http(s) inputs whose WHATWG path/query/fragment changed, all of them through a backslash; no other way to alter the path was found and nothing panicked. The module's central promise ('path ... never rewritten', 'copied byte for byte') therefore has one hole. Low probability in the main flow (claim URLs come from server config), but it is exactly the property the docs guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject '\\' (and ideally the other characters RFC 3986 forbids in an authority: space is already rejected; add < > " { } | ^ `) with QrError::InvalidUrl, or for http(s) end the authority at the first of '/', '\\', '?', '#'. Add the two inputs above as test cases.

findings.title: DOMAIN + REPORT MISMATCH: to_cmyk_naive reaches 299.6 % ink (report says 280 %) and turns near-black tints into 3-plate builds
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-color/src/cmyk.rs:48-59 (to_cmyk_gcr / to_cmyk_naive); implementer report section 'Things integrators should know'
findings.evidence: Exhaustive scan of all 16.7 M colours in a scratch binary: max total ink 299.60785 % at #000001 -> Cmyk{c:1, m:1, y:0, k:0.996}. Also #010000 -> M100 Y100 K99.6 (299.6 %), #0a0000 -> M100 Y100 K96 (296 %); #0a0000 has L* about 0.6, i.e. visually black, yet the build jumps from K100 (100 %) to 296 % on three plates. The code doc ('never exceeds 300 %') is correct; the report's 'can reach 280 %' is not. This is inherent to the divided formula c=(c'-k)/(1-k), which amplifies tiny channel differences as k->1. It matters here because spine text/background colours come from cover palettes (dark covers are common) and the research table (docs/research/notes/print-requirements.prepress.md:18,48-51,134) lists 'text in K only', 260 % for Onlineprinters express and 270 % for Lulu. The contract only asks for a naive, documented, non-colour-managed conversion, so this is not a contract deviation.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the real maximum (299.6 %) and the near-black behaviour on to_cmyk_naive. For print safety either (a) use the PostScript/ISO 32000 10.3.5 subtractive form C=c'-k, M=m'-k, Y=y'-k, K=k (equals the current result times (1-k); total ink <= 200 %, continuous at black; needs the additive inverse 1-min(1,c+k) to round-trip, so coordinate with ebc-scene's to_srgb_approx), or (b) keep the formula and make the spine/card pipeline snap very dark colours (e.g. L* < 5) to Color::BLACK and always pass text colours through limit_total_ink with the print profile's cap.

findings.title: DOC/BEHAVIOUR MISMATCH: ensure_contrast does not return 'the closest lighter or darker version' - it only searches towards the better extreme and can flip a dark colour to a pale one
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-color/src/contrast.rs:66-94 (ensure_contrast; an addition, not a contract item)
findings.evidence: Scratch probe: ensure_contrast(#2b2b2b, #707070, 3.0) returns #cbcbcb (L* 17.5 -> 81.7, +64 L*, ratio 3.05) although #272727 (-2 L*) already reaches 3.02:1. Likewise #40304a on #70708c -> #dbc7e7 (+60 L*) where 6 L* darker suffices. On 900 000 random (fg, bg, min in {3, 4.5, 7}) cases, 25 902 (2.9 %) had a solution more than 5 L* closer in the opposite direction. The guarantee itself holds (0 violations whenever black/white can reach the ratio). The existing test only checks the 'towards white' case and a loose '< 4.5 + 0.2' bound, so it cannot catch this.
findings.suggested_fix: Search both directions in 1 L* steps and return the candidate with the smaller |dL*| (tie: towards the better extreme), or change the first doc sentence to say the colour moves towards whichever of black/white contrasts more with the background, which may be far from the original. Add the #2b2b2b/#707070 case as a test.

overall:
Both crates are sound; I found no critical or major problem, and no contract deviation: every name and signature promised in docs/architecture.md is present with the promised behaviour.

Domain verification, all confirmed independently:
- sRGB transfer function, D65 white, Lab conversion, WCAG luminance and contrast, and CIEDE2000 (all 34 Sharma pairs) are correct.
- Palette extraction is deterministic and bit-identical between native and wasm32.
- QR symbols are spec-conformant: an independent decoder (zbar) reads every mode mix and EC level, capacities match the ISO table, the quiet zone is 4 modules, and orientation is right.
- rects() and to_path() are exact: exact cover, bit-identical shared edges, consistent winding.
- The SVG is well-formed and renders to the same matrix.
- For http(s) URLs the path, query and fragment are never altered, with one exception: a backslash.

The four findings are all minor:
1. normalize_url also upper-cases the scheme and authority of non-http schemes (opds://, custom app schemes), where handlers treat the host as case-sensitive. The doc comment also states the phone-camera behaviour as fact while the research marks it unverified.
2. A backslash in an http(s) URL lets the path be upper-cased under browser parsing.
3. to_cmyk_naive reaches 299.6 % ink, not the 280 % the report states, and turns visually black tints into three-plate builds.
4. ensure_contrast's doc promises "the closest" variant but it searches one direction only; dark text can flip to pale.

Other report inaccuracies are trivial: the raster round trip uses 22 payloads, not 21. The remaining claims I checked hold (test counts, Lab round trip, capacity points, version table, wasm identity).

Test quality is good: assertions are specific and decoded text, version, level and mask are compared. The only test that cannot fail on its stated subject is quiet_zone_matters_to_the_decoder_but_two_modules_still_work, which never shows the quiet zone mattering. The two self-generated pins (HELLO WORLD matrix, cover palette) are disclosed as such. The URL path-preservation property is tested on four hand-picked inputs only; a small fuzz like the one I ran would close finding 2.

Integrators should keep two disclosed behaviours in mind: palette may return fewer than k swatches, and a scanned code decodes to normalize_url(url), not the raw URL.

Not verified: the Android case-sensitivity statement in finding 1 and the GS1 0.396 mm module figure, because the web-search budget was exhausted.
